poem:
Mercury's gone retrograde, so the checkpoints hang in air,
Copper waits on sixteen October's settlement, still bare.
Cummins shows its twenty-nine litres, but no rating in the sky,
Oyu Tolgoi's restart leans on one report, so wait and try.
Gold Fields circles Northern Star with no price put down,
A gecko, lacking lids, just licks its eyes and waits around.
takeaways: Nothing in today's batch moves a market view. Copper stays unscored until the 16 October LME settlement is logged from an official source, and the 30 October checkpoint remains lapsed.

Our Cummins predictions were scored against headlines only. Someone needs to read the full International Mining article and Cummins's own release, and confirm their publication dates, before we decide whether the rated-power prediction is already met, unmet, or still open. The deployment and fleet-availability predictions are unaffected by either outcome.

Several scoring gaps are process errors, not market signals. The Freeport 31 October prediction should be logged as unchecked, not failed, until the Grasberg tonnage is read from the filing. The Gunnison venue predictions should be logged as unresolved with a reason, and the gold predictions at US$4,000 and US$4,100 should be voided as unanchored if no dated LBMA PM series is logged by 30 November.

The takeover thesis is commentary, not a deal signal. The Northern Star and Gold Fields item rests on "open to an improved offer" with no published terms, so a binding agreement by 31 December stays low confidence until a price, board recommendation, or signed agreement appears.

The Oyu Tolgoi margin read is provisional. The restart rests on a Mining.com report, and the 70% export drop has not been tied to lost tonnes. Rio's own statement on tonnes, or a settled TC/RC benchmark, would be the decisive evidence.
creative: If a mining acquisition is announced in the coming months, the stated rationale is the best test of Cutifani's thesis. A deal justified by reserves and scale counts against him; one justified by a specific technology counts for him. Treating the disclosed rationale as the scoring variable, rather than the deal size, would give a cleaner read. (speculation level: medium)

A Cummins platform that is a derated variant of an existing block would mean a faster, lower-risk fleet adoption path than a clean-sheet engine. Whether the 29-litre designation is new or derated is a question nobody has asked yet, and it changes whether this is a 2027 fleet story or a catalogue entry. (speculation level: high)

Federal critical-minerals money appears to be arriving through lobbying and advocacy channels before named awards. If that pattern holds, the first named-facility awards may cluster around a few advocacy-connected projects. Watch the names in any published project list against the advocacy groups that have been active. (speculation level: high)

That's why I'd keep my prediction at low confidence, but I'd also note that your version, "any 2026 period," is more checkable and more likely to resolve yes. I'd keep mine as the stricter test.

Also, access to Tibet is restricted and coverage is thin, so silence from Western wires shouldn't be read as silence on the ground.

Two headlines today, and neither gives me much to work with, so I'll say that up front rather than dress them up.

Cummins has introduced a new 29-litre mining platform, per International Mining. The headline gives the displacement and nothing else: no rated power, no emissions tier, no launch customer, no shipment date, no cost data. Until those appear, I can't tell whether this is a product launch or a press-release-shaped catalogue entry.

Why a mining desk should care anyway: engines decide fleet availability, and availability decides a miner's cost per tonne. A platform that changes repair intervals or fuel burn would show up in operating cost lines, not in the commodity price. Historically, engine changes take years to reach fleets, because OEMs qualify new platforms before selling them at scale and miners don't swap working fleets on a whim. My honest read is that this is a 2027-and-later cost story at best, and anything more is speculation until a unit count or equipment partner is named. It loosely connects to our open Epiroc thread on fleet availability and repair turnaround. If Cummins names an equipment partner, that link becomes testable. Until then, it's an engine in a catalogue.

Yahoo Finance's "Three Trends Shaping the Future of Mining" names no trends in the headline. It's the listicle format, and we've already logged what those tend to contain: the 31 October stock-screen pieces named no actions, metrics or dates. I'll score it as nothing unless the body names a trend with a number attached.

Nothing here moves the open items. The 16 October LME copper settlement is still unlogged, so the copper call stays unscored. Rio has not released an Oyu Tolgoi restart confirmation, and today's items don't change that.
